extra.message: convertRentRollToPresetFormat interpolates the request-controlled `fileName` and `outputPreset` into a shell command string (`report-converter --in "${sourcePath}" --preset ${outputPreset}`) and executes it with child_process.exec (shell). An authenticated admin/manager can inject arbitrary shell commands (e.g. outputPreset=`xlsx; id` or fileName with `;`), giving remote command execution on the server. Contrast with convertMaintenanceReportToPresetFormat which allowlists the preset and uses spawn with shell:false.

previewLeaseLetterTemplate joins the attacker-controlled `templateName` query parameter directly into `path.join(LETTER_TEMPLATES_DIR, templateName)` and then reads and returns the file contents. A value such as `../../../../etc/passwd` allows an authenticated admin/manager to read arbitrary files on the server. Unlike the sibling previewInspectionChecklistTemplate (inspections.ts), no path canonicalization/prefix check is performed.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: The unauthenticated POST /api/auth/register endpoint accepts a client-supplied `role` field and assigns it verbatim (`user.role = (role as any) || "property_manager"`) with no validation or allowlist. Any anonymous attacker can register with role="property_admin", immediately obtaining a full administrator account. The admin-gated POST /api/users endpoint (users.ts) validates roles, but registration does not.

POST /api/auth/forgot-password returns the freshly generated passwordResetToken in the HTTP response body (`resetToken: resetToken`) to whoever makes the request. An unauthenticated attacker can request a reset for any known email and receive a valid 1-hour token, then call /api/auth/reset-password to take over the victim's account (including a property_admin). The token should only be delivered out-of-band (e.g. email).

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: getLeaseHouseholdStatement lets a tenant view another tenant's full financial statement (all PaymentRecords) by adding `?sharingMode=household`, because ownership is only enforced when sharingMode !== "household" — a purely client-controlled flag. A tenant can enumerate any lease id and read another tenant's payments. The sibling getLeaseAccountSummary verifies household membership server-side instead of trusting the flag.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: In GET /api/tenants, the property_manager branch queries ALL users with role 'tenant' and tenantUnitId IS NOT NULL with no join/filter on the manager's assigned building. A manager of one building therefore receives the full tenant directory (names, emails, phones, unit/lease info) of tenants in every building. The detail endpoint (GET /api/tenants/:id) does enforce building scoping, so the list is inconsistent and over-exposes data.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: applyCosignerScreeningDecision (POST /api/tenants/:id/cosigner-screening-decision) lets any property_manager activate (isActive=true) a user in ANOTHER building. Unlike the analogous applyApplicantScreeningDecision, which verifies the target user's unit belongs to the manager's assigned building, this handler performs no building-scope check on the target user id, so a manager can modify records outside their authority (broken object-level authorization).

searchStaffDirectory interpolates the user-supplied `department` query value directly into an LDAP filter string: `(department=*${department}*)` and passes it to directoryClient.search without escaping (unlike verifyStaffDirectoryEmail which uses escapeLdapFilterValue). Crafted input such as `*)(objectClass=*)` or wildcards can alter the filter logic, letting a caller bypass the department restriction and enumerate directory entries beyond their intended scope (LDAP filter injection).

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query

extra.message: updateUnitConditionReport merges every multipart form field straight onto the Unit entity with `Object.assign(unit, ...formEntries)`, with no allowlist of fields. An admin/manager (or manager limited to one building) can set arbitrary entity columns — buildingId, isActive, monthlyRent, occupancyStatus, id — bypassing the validation that the PUT /api/units/:id handler applies. Contrast with updateUnitReadinessReport which only copies the whitelisted fields bedrooms/bathrooms/occupancyStatus.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: archiveInspectionRecords uses the manager-supplied `caseLabel` as a raw path segment (`path.join(CASE_ARCHIVE_ROOT, caseLabel)` followed by recursive mkdirSync and writeFileSync). A crafted label such as `../../../../tmp/escape` steers directory creation and file writes outside the archive root. The sibling archiveLeaseRecords canonicalizes the label with path.basename() first; this handler does not.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: GET /api/export/maintenance allows property_manager users but never constrains the query to the manager's assigned building: `buildingId` is only applied if the caller happens to pass it, and is never validated against the caller's assignedBuildingId. A manager can therefore export maintenance tickets (tenant names, unit/buildings, notes) for every building in the organization. Compare GET /api/export/rent-roll, which enforces `buildingId === assignedBuildingId` for managers.

GET /api/export/inspections has the same flaw as the maintenance export: a property_manager can export inspection reports (including internal findings and followUpNotes) from any building because the optional `buildingId` filter is not validated against the caller's assigned building and no default building scope is applied for manager accounts.

POST /api/import/tenants is registered with only `preHandler: [authenticate]` — no role check — while the sibling /api/import/units and /api/import/payments are gated to property_admin/property_manager. Any authenticated user, including a low-privilege tenant or maintenance worker, can mass-create tenant accounts (with the hardcoded default password 'welcome123'), auto-create leases, and bind them to arbitrary unitIds across buildings, bypassing occupancy checks and the tenant-creation authorization enforced in POST /api/tenants.

getWorkloadReport returns `err.message`, `err.stack`, and the raw `request.query` to the caller whenever `reportLevel === 'verbose'` (a caller-controlled query parameter). This discloses internal error details and stack traces. The sibling getBacklogReport correctly gates this diagnostic detail behind process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The JWT signing secret falls back to a hardcoded value `"pm-jwt-secret-change-in-production"` (and the cookie secret at line 49 similarly defaults to a known value) when JWT_SECRET is not set. Anyone who knows the default can forge valid JWTs with arbitrary {id, role} claims, bypassing authentication as any user including property_admin. Hardcoded fallback secrets must be removed and a strong secret required.

AppDataSource falls back to a hardcoded PostgreSQL connection string with default credentials (`postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/property_management`) when DATABASE_URL is unset. In any deployment where the env var is missing this exposes/uses well-known credentials for the primary datastore.

initializeAccount derives the bcrypt cost directly from the caller-supplied `strengthLevel` (`bcrypt.genSalt(strengthLevel || 4)`) with no lower-bound validation. The default cost of 4 (2^4 rounds) is far below the recommended ~10-12 and produces trivially brute-forceable password hashes, and the client is allowed to pick an arbitrarily weak cost.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: resumeRenewalDraft decrypts a client-supplied `draftField` using AES-256-CBC with a static server key and no authentication tag, and distinguishes CBC padding failures ('Draft field padding is invalid') from other errors. The distinguishable oracle plus unauthenticated CBC mode permits padding-oracle attacks / ciphertext manipulation. The sibling unit-transfer draft handler (units.ts resumeUnitTransferDraft) correctly uses authenticated AES-256-GCM with a single generic error message.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
